questions.text: A grammar is LL(1) only if, for every non-terminal with two productions A -> alpha and A -> beta, which condition holds?
options: FIRST(alpha) and FIRST(beta) are disjoint, and if one derives epsilon its FIRST is disjoint from FOLLOW(A)
questions.explain: A single lookahead token must uniquely select a production, so the FIRST sets must not overlap, and an epsilon-deriving alternative must not conflict with FOLLOW(A). Left recursion always breaks LL(1).

questions.text: Which containment among parser classes is correct?
options: LR(0) subset SLR(1) subset LALR(1) subset CLR(1)
CLR(1) subset LALR(1) subset SLR(1) subset LR(0)
SLR(1) subset LR(0) subset LALR(1) subset CLR(1)
LALR(1) subset SLR(1) subset CLR(1) subset LR(0)
questions.explain: Each class strictly contains the previous one in parsing power. CLR(1) (canonical LR) is the most powerful, and LALR(1) merges CLR states with identical cores, which can introduce reduce-reduce conflicts CLR would not have.

questions.text: Merging LR(1) states with identical cores to build an LALR(1) table can introduce which kind of conflict?
questions.explain: State merging can only widen lookahead sets, which can make two reductions valid on the same token. It can never create a new shift-reduce conflict.

questions.text: Which class of machine is sufficient to implement a lexical analyser?
questions.explain: Tokens are described by regular expressions, so a finite automaton suffices. Parsing needs a pushdown automaton because it must handle nesting.

questions.text: Which attribute kind can be evaluated in a single bottom-up pass during LR parsing without restructuring the grammar?
questions.explain: Synthesised attributes flow from children to parent, matching the order reductions occur in bottom-up parsing. Inherited attributes flow downwards and generally need an L-attributed definition with top-down evaluation.

questions.text: Live variable analysis is which kind of data flow problem?
questions.explain: Liveness asks whether a value may be used later, so information flows backwards from uses and merges with union. Available expressions is the forward, intersection counterpart.

questions.text: How many three-address instructions, each with at most one operator, are needed to evaluate a = b * c + b * c - d without any common subexpression elimination?
questions.explain: t1 = b * c; t2 = b * c; t3 = t1 + t2; a = t3 - d. That is 4 instructions. With CSE the second multiplication disappears, leaving 3.

questions.text: Under static (lexical) scoping, the binding of a free variable in a function is determined by:
options: The call chain at run time
The textual nesting of the function in the source
The order in which functions are declared in the file
The size of the activation record
questions.explain: Static scoping resolves names by enclosing source blocks, decidable at compile time. Resolving by the run-time call chain is dynamic scoping.
